record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Relative isoperimetric profile of the cube
record.original_question: Let Q be the unit cube in R^N, N≥3, and for 0≤t≤1 define f_N(t)=\inf\{P(S): S\subset Q measurable, |S|=t\}, where P(S) is the relative perimeter inside Q. Is there an explicit formula for f_N(t) analogous to the known two-dimensional formula for the square? In particular, is f_N(t) identically equal to 1 for t near 1/2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10.1 ([21]). Is there a formula similar to (10.2) for fN(t) when N ≥ 3? In particular, is it true that fN(t) ≡ 1 near t = 1/2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N\ge 3$ and let $Q=(0,1)^N$ denote the open unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^N$. For a measurable set $S\subset Q$ of finite perimeter, let $P(S)$ denote the relative perimeter of $S$ inside $Q$, i.e. the $(N-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of $\partial^* S \cap Q$ (the reduced boundary of $S$ intersected with the interior of the cube). For $t\in[0,1]$ define the relative isoperimetric profile of the cube
$$f_N(t)\;=\;\inf\bigl\{P(S)\,:\, S\subset Q\text{ measurable},\ |S|=t\bigr\}.$$
In dimension $N=2$ (the unit square) an explicit closed-form formula for $f_2(t)$ is known, given piecewise in terms of $t$, and in particular $f_2(t)\equiv 1$ for $t$ in a neighborhood of $1/2$ (with the optimal sets being half-squares).

(a) Determine an explicit formula for $f_N(t)$ for all $t\in[0,1]$ when $N\ge 3$, analogous to the two-dimensional case.

(b) In particular, prove or disprove: there exists $\varepsilon_N>0$ such that $f_N(t)\equiv 1$ for all $t\in[\tfrac12-\varepsilon_N,\tfrac12+\varepsilon_N]$.
artifact.category_tag: Relative isoperimetric profile of the cube
artifact.status_search_result: Part (b) has been established: Glaudo (2023, arXiv:2305.20051) proved that for every dimension $d$, subsets of the unit cube with volume sufficiently close to $1/2$ have relative perimeter at least $1$, so $f_N(t)\equiv 1$ in a neighborhood of $t=1/2$ (settling a conjecture of Brezis–Bruckstein). The full explicit formula for $f_N(t)$ for all $t$ in dimensions $N\ge 3$ remains open; partial results and bounds appear in related work such as arXiv:2302.04382 and arXiv:2403.06602.

status_evidence.title: On the Isoperimetric Profile of the Hypercube (Glaudo)
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that a subset of the hypercube (0,1)^d with volume sufficiently close to 1/2 has (relative) perimeter greater than or equal to 1.
status_evidence.claim: f_N(t) = 1 for t near 1/2 is established in every dimension.

status_evidence.title: On the relative isoperimetric problem for the cube
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the relative isoperimetric problem for the cube in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The full explicit formula for f_N(t) remains under active investigation, no closed form analogous to the 2D case is established.

status_evidence.title: Isoperimetric Inequalities on Slabs with applications to Cubes
status_evidence.snippet: Provides isoperimetric inequalities relevant to cubes; explicit profile not given.
status_evidence.claim: No complete explicit formula for f_N is known in dimension N>=3.
